rationale: Correct the existing Third Coast Infrastructure record in place and map ArcLight's census label Third Coast Infrastructure (CV) to that canonical company. ArcLight's current portfolio distinguishes Third Coast CV as Current from legacy Third Coast Midstream as Realized, while its January 2023 continuation-fund release states that ArcLight 3C SPV, L.P. acquired an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V, L.P. affiliate's remaining 25.1% interest in Third Coast Super Holdings, LLC in July 2022. The existing undifferentiated active ArcLight period beginning in 2019 must therefore become a realized Fund V period ending in 2022, followed by a new active ArcLight 3C SPV period beginning in 2022. Current company, manager and institutional evidence supports preserving J.P. Morgan Asset Management / Infrastructure Investments Fund (IIF) as an active co-owner from 2021, but the approximately 50% disclosed in the 2021 transaction applied to subsidiary Lighthouse Super Holdings, LLC and must not be stored as an exact parent-platform stake. Third Coast Super Holdings, Third Coast Infrastructure, the legacy Third Coast Midstream / American Midstream business, Lighthouse and individual infrastructure assets remain one manager-level platform boundary. No later platform sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 15, 2026. ArcLight 3C SPV is stored as the factual vehicle with a null fund link because no matching production Fund row exists; this avoids inventing a dependency while preserving the researched vehicle identity.

afterImage.name: Third Coast Infrastructure
afterImage.description: Third Coast Infrastructure is a Houston-headquartered offshore and coastal midstream platform operating natural gas, crude oil and NGL gathering, transmission, processing and floating-production infrastructure across the U.S. Gulf Coast and Gulf of Mexico. The platform traces to American Midstream Partners, was taken private by ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V in 2019, added J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund as a significant minority co-owner in 2021, and moved ArcLight's remaining 25.1% interest into ArcLight 3C SPV in July 2022. Current public materials list Third Coast CV as an ArcLight investment and identify a J.P. Morgan Asset Management-advised vehicle as an owner; exact current parent-platform ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. As of May 2026, company materials described approximately 1,900 pipeline miles, one gas processing plant and interests in four offshore floating production systems. No platform-level exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

milestones.event: American Midstream Partners, the predecessor to the current Third Coast platform, was formed in August 2009.
ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V affiliates completed the take-private of American Midstream Partners, which converted into Third Coast Midstream, LLC on the same date.

An Infrastructure Investments Fund affiliate made a significant minority investment in Third Coast Super Holdings, adding J.P. Morgan Asset Management's infrastructure strategy as a co-owner of the platform.

Third Coast completed the sale of an approximately 50% interest in subsidiary Lighthouse Super Holdings to a global infrastructure vehicle; the percentage does not establish the buyer's exact stake in the canonical parent platform.
ArcLight 3C SPV acquired ArcLight Fund V's remaining 25.1% interest in Third Coast Super Holdings, moving ArcLight's investment into a continuation vehicle.
Third Coast Super Holdings announced a $25 million loan upsize and repricing at the infrastructure subsidiary level.

Third Coast announced a $125 million term-loan upsize and described an active platform with approximately 1,900 pipeline miles, one gas processing plant and interests in four offshore floating production systems.
